title: Pin coercion and resolver graceful-degradation policy for ambiguous selectors
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: customers can specify model pins in many formats (plain tag like 'stable', semver ranges like 'v1.x', exact semver 'v1.2.3', and commit hashes/short-hashes). Historically the server-side resolver accepted a broad set of inputs but SDK clients have divergent behaviours which has produced surprising rollouts and silent fallbacks. We need a documented, deterministic coercion and fallback policy that: 1) minimizes surprise for users; 2) preserves backwards compatibility for common pins; 3) allows safe progressive rollout (canary) of pinned variants; 4) provides telemetry to detect ambiguous matches.

Proposal summary: Introduce a three-stage resolver strategy enforced across API and SDKs: 1) Exact match phase (highest precedence): exact semver or full commit hash; 2) Deterministic expansion phase: semver range and tag resolution following a deterministic catalog rule (catalog priority: release > channel tag > user tag), expanded to a ranked list; 3) Fallback/coercion phase (lowest precedence): short-hash expansion and best-effort semver coercion (e.g., implicit patch from v1.2 => v1.2.latest) only when caller opts in via an explicit pin-coercion header/option. The default server behavior will reject ambiguous short-hashes unless the request includes opt-in header or SDK flag. This reduces silent behavior while maintaining ergonomics for interactive use.

Requirements and goals:
- Deterministic, documented precedence so clients can reason about which model version will serve.
- No silent downgrades: if resolver cannot deterministically pick a single matching model, respond with resolvable error and suggested candidates unless caller allowed coercion.
- Backwards compatibility: existing simple tag usage remains unchanged for tags we treat as channels (e.g., 'stable', 'edge'), but ambiguous tags that overlap must be surfaced.
- SDK-level dry-run: SDKs will offer a resolve() call that returns the resolved artifact and a resolution_trace for logging/telemetry.
- Server-side audit: record resolution path (selector, resolved id, fallback steps) in request logs and console UI for debugging.

Out of scope for this ticket: changes to catalog naming policies, automated renaming of tags, or new catalog UI components.
acceptance_criteria: Server rejects ambiguous short-hash pins by default and returns candidate list with HTTP 409 and resolver_hint payload (stringified list)
SDKs (JS + Python + Go) expose a resolve(selector, options) API that returns resolved_id and resolution_trace as strings
Resolver precedence documented in docs page: exact > semver-expansion > tag-channel > short-hash (opt-in)
Telemetry events include selector, final_resolved_id, resolution_latency_ms, and coercion_used flag
Rollout tests show zero regression for 95th latency percentile for model resolution path under load
implementation_plan: Design: finalize resolver precedence matrix and error codes (this ticket)
Server: implement strict short-hash rejection unless opt-in header presence detected (runtime change)
Server: attach resolution_trace to request logs and event stream (audit fields as strings)
SDK: add resolve() API and opt-in pin_coercion option; propagate header 'X-Redwood-Pin-Coercion: true' when opted-in
Docs: publish resolver behavioral contract and examples for common pins
QA: integration tests across catalog permutations and chaos tests for concurrent tag updates
Telemetry: update event schema and dashboard to expose coercion rate and ambiguous-pin error rates
testing_notes: Unit: resolver unit matrix covering exact semver, semver range, tag, full-hash, short-hash (ambiguous vs unique)
Integration: server+sdk resolve() smoke tests returning deterministic resolution_trace strings
Load: synthetic traffic to resolver endpoint to measure added latency (target <5ms p95 added)
Chaos: simulate a tag flip during resolution window to verify that resolution is consistent (snapshot isolation)

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: breaking scripts that rely on short-hash implicit expansion. Mitigation: default off, provide clear error with candidate list and one-click coercion suggestion in Console
Risk: catalog naming collisions between channel tags and user tags. Mitigation: add catalog-level disambiguation logs and a migration playbook for customers
Risk: added latency in resolution. Mitigation: caching of resolved ids per selector with TTL and prewarm in SDK resolve() path
